historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr tempered by fee algorithm (NUG 6-7% + RevPAR 3-3.5% guided for FY2026; total revenue grows slower than fees because reimbursements and the ownership segment dilute it). Equity CAGR is undefined: book equity is negative.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR cannot be computed (shareholders' equity negative since FY2019 from debt-funded buybacks). 5-year CAGRs start from the FY2020 COVID trough (revenue $4.3B, EPS -$2.58) and are not meaningful; the 3-year figures (FY2022-FY2025) and the FY2019-FY2025 6-year revenue CAGR of 4.1% bracket the real trend.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = OCF - PP&E capex - SBC add-back - equity-award withholding taxes (capitalized software not available in the CSV for FY2022, so excluded from both endpoints for consistency): FY2022 $1,422M -> FY2025 $1,786M = 7.9% 3yr CAGR vs 7.3% on reported FCF. SBC has grown slightly slower than cash flow (FY2022 $162M -> FY2025 $170M), so SBC is not eating the reported growth here.

scenario_narratives.base: Hilton keeps executing its asset-light algorithm: net unit growth of 6-7% in FY2026 (record pipeline of ~3,850 hotels / 541k rooms, half under construction) fading toward 4-5% by the early 2030s as the base grows, system-wide RevPAR of 3-3.5% in FY2026 normalising toward 2-3%, and the ownership/reimbursement drag shrinking as a share of revenue so GAAP EBITDA margin rises from 23.8% (FY2025) to about 28.5% by FY2035. SBC stays ~2% of revenue, capex ~1.6%, and the Honors co-brand float contributes a modest working-capital tailwind. Value is discounted at a uniform 8.5% USD WACC with 3% terminal growth; Gordon binds below the 20x cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: The axes that matter are pipeline conversion and RevPAR durability. In the bull case the 541k-room pipeline converts at 7%+ NUG for several more years, conversion brands (Spark, Curio, Tapestry) and international markets (India, Middle East, Japan) keep the signings pace ahead of openings, business transient demand (+5.7% in Q2-2026) sustains RevPAR of 3-4%, and the growing share of fee income pushes GAAP EBITDA margin past 30%. Hilton Honors' 200M members widen the direct-booking advantage, and the credit-card float captures 20% of incremental revenue.
scenario_narratives.bear: Lodging is classically cyclical and Hilton now carries ~4x net debt/EBITDA with no equity cushion. The bear case is a 2027-28 recession: RevPAR falls 6-8% (a 2009-scale shock, not 2020), fee income drops with it, developer construction financing tightens so NUG slips toward 4%, and Hilton concedes owner-favourable fee adjustments (already flagged in Q2-2026 commentary) to defend conversion share against Marriott, IHG, Wyndham and Choice. Margins compress to ~22.5% at the trough and recover only to 26%. Buybacks pause but debt service is maintained; the terminal cap is cut to 15x for a cyclical fee stream on a levered balance sheet.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Hilton is one of the best fee-based business models in the market: capital-light, high incremental margins, a loyalty network with 200M members and a record development pipeline. The valuation question is not quality but price. The house DCF expenses SBC, deducts the $12.3B of net debt that funded the buybacks, discounts at a uniform 8.5% and caps the terminal multiple at 20x; on those terms the market price sits well above intrinsic value and implies either a materially lower required return or a longer runway of 7%+ growth than the base case grants. The negative book equity is a capital-allocation artefact, not a distress signal, but it means the entire equity value rests on the durability of the fee stream through a downturn.
key_risks_to_valuation: Travel-demand recession: RevPAR and fee income fall together; with ~4x leverage and no equity cushion, buybacks pause and the multiple derates
Pipeline-to-open conversion slows if developer financing tightens (higher-for-longer rates)
Owner-favourable fee concessions to hold conversion share against Marriott/IHG/Wyndham/Choice compress fee margin
Premium multiple (trailing P/E ~46x, ~40x owner FCF) leaves little room for execution misses
GAAP EBITDA basis includes zero-margin cost reimbursements; a change in the reimbursed-cost net loss (Honors, marketing funds) moves the modelled margin without changing fees
Discount-rate sensitivity: a terminal-heavy, long-duration fee stream loses value quickly as required return rises

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 253.54-358.00
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 0001585689): FY2025 10-K filed 2026-02-11, Q2-2026 10-Q filed 2026-07-28; HLT_Metrics.csv (core_metrics) for the history; kpis table for buybacks, cash taxes, equity-award taxes
data_sources.qualitative: HLT_Analysis.json (2026-09-29): Q2-2026 guidance (RevPAR +3.0-3.5%, Adjusted EBITDA $4.04-4.08B, NUG 6-7%, ~$3.5B capital return), pipeline, bull/bear axes

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: share-based compensation add-back $170M (us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation) plus $72M cash withholding taxes on net-share settlement (us-gaap:PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation, financing activities). Hilton publishes no combined figure in its Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation (that line is the $170M expense only), so the two are summed.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases $3,182M; H1-2026 $1,787M (us-gaap:PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock). The flat share count is fully funded: Hilton retires ~10M shares a year, far more than SBC issues. Buybacks are value-neutral in this model (SBC is expensed; count held flat).
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted ~227.0M at 30 June 2026: 10-Q cover 225.06M basic at 23 July 2026 rolled back to quarter-end at the disclosed ~0.86M/month buyback pace (~225.5M) plus ~1.5M dilutive RSU/PSU/options (Q2-2026 weighted diluted 229M vs basic). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Q2-2026 10-Q, 30 June 2026: long-term debt incl. finance leases $12,719M + current maturities $624M = $13,343M (us-gaap:LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations + ...Current; no double count of the current portion), less cash $1,009M. Finance lease liabilities ($325M) sit in debt because their cost (ROU amortisation in D&A, $8M interest) is outside EBITDA. Operating lease liabilities ($851M at FY2025) are EXCLUDED because operating lease cost ($145M/yr payments) is inside EBITDA under US GAAP.
inputs.reported_fcf_basis: FY2025 OCF $2,129M less capex for property & equipment $101M less capitalized software $84M = $1,944M (Hilton's own free-cash-flow definition). The Metrics CSV FreeCashFlow of $2,028M deducts PP&E only. Contract acquisition costs (key money) are classified INSIDE operating activities by Hilton, so they are already in OCF and need no further deduction.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST, Sep-2026), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.0-1.1 for a fee-based lodging franchisor -> cost of equity ~9.2-9.7%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.3% (FY2025 interest expense $620M on ~$11.7B average debt), ~4.0% after tax. Market weights: equity ~$73B vs debt $13.3B -> D/V ~15%. WACC = 0.85 x 9.4% + 0.15 x 4.0% = ~8.6%, rounded to 8.5%. Held IDENTICAL across scenarios so risk is charged once, through the driver paths and probability weights, not twice through per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: One treatment: operating leases (owned/leased hotel segment) are an operating cost inside EBITDA and their liabilities are NOT added to net debt; finance leases are in net debt and their ROU amortisation/interest are outside EBITDA. Never both.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interests $28M (30 June 2026) deducted once in the equity bridge; flows are consolidated. Immaterial (<0.1% of EV).
inputs.tax_basis: Cash tax rate 25% on EBIT, unlevered: between the 21% federal statutory rate and the 29.5% FY2025 GAAP effective rate (state, foreign, unrecognised-tax-benefit accruals); FY2025 cash taxes paid $523M on pretax income $2,072M = 25.2%. The interest tax shield is carried in the after-tax cost of debt in WACC, not in the flows.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: operating company, US, asset-light franchisor). Negative book equity (-$6.3B at Q2-2026) is the product of a decade of debt-funded buybacks against a fee stream that does not need the capital; it is not a routing trigger (no distress, no going-concern issue, interest cover ~4.5x on GAAP EBITDA) and the equity-CAGR growth anchor is simply undefined for this ticker, so revenue and owner-FCF CAGRs are used instead. EBITDA in the CSV is GAAP operating income + D&A on GROSS revenue (including ~$3.5B+ of zero-margin cost reimbursements from managed and franchised properties); it is ~$0.8B below Hilton's 'Adjusted EBITDA' because it carries the reimbursed-cost net loss, SBC and other add-backs. The margin paths below are on that GAAP basis and must not be compared with Hilton's adjusted-EBITDA guidance without that bridge. Owner FCF (last_fcf) is levered (after $648M cash interest) and is an anchor only; the projections are unlevered from components and net debt is deducted at the end. FY0 is FY2025; year 1 is FY2026 discounted a full period even though nine months have elapsed (slightly conservative). Working capital: Hilton runs a structural float from Hilton Honors co-brand card prepayments and deferred revenue (+$194M in FY2025 alone; contract liabilities $2.35B), captured conservatively at 15% of the revenue change in the base case versus ~40% observed in FY2025. Interest income is immaterial against $12.3B of net debt and is not stripped. Price is the 2026-09-28 regular close, not an after-hours print.

bear.narrative: A 2027-28 travel recession (RevPAR -6 to -8%, as in 2009 scale rather than 2020 scale), developer financing tightens so NUG slips toward 4%, owner-favourable fee concessions to hold conversion share compress margin, and the recovery settles at a lower long-run growth and a 15x terminal cap for a cyclical fee stream on a levered balance sheet.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +7.0%: H1-2026 revenue +7.6% YoY, Q2 +6.5%, with guidance raised to RevPAR +3.0-3.5% and NUG 6-7%. Decelerates 0.5pp/yr as NUG normalises toward 5% and RevPAR toward inflation; 3% terminal.
base.margin_rationale: GAAP EBITDA margin FY2025 23.8%, H1-2026 26.0% (H1-2025 24.0%). FY2026 25.5% ties to Adjusted EBITDA guidance $4.04-4.08B less the ~$0.8B GAAP bridge. Expands ~0.5pp/yr early as fee revenue outgrows reimbursements and the ownership segment, flattening at 28.5% by FY2035 (mature).
base.capex_rationale: PP&E $101M + capitalized software $84M = 1.5% of FY2025 revenue; FY2024 1.8%. Held at 1.6%. D&A 1.5% (FY2025 $177M).
base.narrative: Fee algorithm intact: mid-single-digit unit growth plus low-single-digit RevPAR, margin drifting up with mix, all FCF returned.

bull.narrative: Record 541k-room pipeline converts at 7%+ NUG for longer, international (India, Middle East, APAC) and conversion brands keep the runway open, RevPAR holds 3-4%, fee mix drives GAAP EBITDA margin past 30%, and the Honors float captures 20% of growth.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because travel demand is highly cyclical, net debt/EBITDA is ~4x with negative book equity (no balance-sheet cushion if fees fall), and Q2-2026 commentary already flagged owner fee concessions. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it requires sustained 7%+ NUG, RevPAR re-acceleration AND margin expansion beyond 30% together, and the current price already discounts most of that path (trailing P/E ~46x).

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
